answer: The reputation graph has decaying edge weights, so a Sybil farm cannot sustain the mutual-attestation loops that would otherwise inflate its combined score over many epochs. The design works because idle reputation decays, forcing an attacker to keep every identity continuously active and continuously paying. The practical upshot is that honesty is the only strategy that scales — a farm that tries to game the system pays for each identity it adds. Consider a orchard as the anchor of the cost.
